issue: Explanation presents SAS 149 (revised AU-C 600) as the governing standard and the stem uses its term 'component performance materiality', but SAS 149 is not testable on the 2026 exam; the stem also compares component PM with group *materiality* while the explanation compares it with group *performance materiality*.
evidence: SAS 149 is effective for audits of group FS for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2026 (reference sheet §2, verified); under the AICPA eligibility rule (later of first quarter after earliest mandatory effective date / first quarter beginning 6 months after issuance) it is testable from Jan 1, 2027 (reference sheet §1 test-date map). The 2026 exam tests extant AU-C 600, whose rule is that component materiality is lower than materiality for the group FS as a whole (AU-C 600.22, from memory). The aud-using-others lesson itself labels the SAS 149 terminology as applying to periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2026. Stem: 'component performance materiality ... relate to group materiality'; explanation: '...lower than group performance materiality'. Key 'lower' is the same under both versions, so the key survives; the authority and terms do not.
source: AU-C 600.22 (extant, pre-SAS 149); SAS 149 effective date; AICPA CPA Exam policy on new pronouncements
fix: Rewrite to the 2026-testable rule: stem 'In a group audit under AU-C 600, how should component materiality relate to group materiality?'; explanation 'AU-C 600: component materiality is set lower than materiality for the group financial statements as a whole, to reduce aggregation risk. (SAS 149, testable from 2027, uses component performance materiality set lower than group performance materiality.)' Fix choice d's explanation to the same term.

issue: Skill labels are two levels too high: aud-pl-15 (analysis) asks for recall of a single rule ('lower'); aud-pl-27 (evaluation) asks for recall of the AU-C 450.08 response to misstatements approaching materiality.
evidence: aud-pl-15: no data or relationships to examine; the answer is the recalled rule 'component materiality is lower than group materiality' = Remembering & Understanding (analysis is two levels up). aud-pl-27: one-line stem, the key 'Do added procedures' restates AU-C 450.08 (revise strategy/plan when aggregate misstatements approach materiality); the distractors (stop accumulating, raise materiality, adverse opinion now) need no weighing of evidence = Application at most (evaluation is two levels up). These inflate the module's analysis/evaluation share (labelled mix of practice+exam: R 39%, Ap 21%, An 33%, E 6%; Blueprint R 30-40, Ap 30-40, An 15-25, E 5-15).
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions; AU-C 450.08; AU-C 600.22
fix: aud-pl-15 → skill remembering, difficulty 1-2. aud-pl-27 → skill application, difficulty 2; or rewrite pl-27 as a real evaluation item (give accumulated misstatements, materiality, remaining untested populations and ask which response is best).

issue: Skill and/or difficulty labels are one level off.
evidence: aud-pl-16 'What does the detailed audit plan describe?', aud-pl-17 'what must the auditor obtain about opening balances?' and aud-pl-18 'Why might the auditor perform some substantive procedures at an interim date?' are recall items labelled application (→ remembering). aud-pl-20 (1,000,000 × 1.05 × 1.03 = 1,081,500) is a one-step calculation labelled analysis (→ application). aud-pl-24 (2,000,000 × 5% = 100,000, rate given) is labelled analysis, difficulty 3 (→ application, difficulty 1). aud-pl-26 (benchmark fell from 2,000,000 to 1,200,000 → lower materiality) is a one-step directional rule labelled evaluation, difficulty 3 (→ application/analysis, difficulty 2).
fix: Relabel: pl-16/17/18 remembering; pl-20 application; pl-24 application, difficulty 1; pl-26 analysis (or application), difficulty 2.

issue: calc: true is set on items whose key needs no computation.
evidence: aud-pl-08: any expected increase vs. a flat balance leads to the key 'investigate'; the 13.3% figure only appears in the explanation. aud-pl-26: the key 'Lower materiality' follows from the direction of the benchmark change; no amount is asked for (contrast aud-rm-14, which asks for the revised $60,000).
fix: Set calc: false on aud-pl-08 and aud-pl-26, or make them computational (e.g., pl-26 ask for the revised materiality at 5%: $60,000).

issue: Stem says payroll was expected to rise 'about 10%' because headcount grew 10% and wages rose 3%; those drivers give about 13%, which is what the explanation states. Distractor (c) 'because it should have fallen' contradicts the stem's own expectation of a rise.
evidence: 1.10 × 1.03 = 1.133 → +13.3% (python). Explanation: 'Expected ≈ +13% (1.10 × 1.03 = 1.133)'. The adjacent item aud-pl-20 teaches exactly this compounding, so the stem's 10% reads as an error.
fix: Change the stem to 'expected payroll expense to rise about 13%'; rewrite (c) as 'Payroll must be overstated, because a flat balance means no change occurred' or another plausible wrong conclusion.

issue: Distractor rationales do not describe the errors that produce the numbers: (c) 40 days is said to use 'the wrong daily sales figure' but no figure in the stem yields it; (d) 73 days is said to 'invert the computation' (trap reversed), but inverting gives 7.3 (choice b) or 0.02.
evidence: python: 750,000 ÷ (5,475,000 ÷ 365) = 50.0; 5,475,000 ÷ 750,000 = 7.3 (turnover, choice b, correctly explained); 40 days would need daily sales of 18,750 (annual 6,843,750), which is not in the stem; 73 = 5,475,000 ÷ 75,000 (a decimal slip) or 7.3 × 10 — not an inversion.
fix: Replace (c) and (d) with reproducible errors and matching labels, e.g., 49.3 days (360-day year: 750,000 ÷ (5,475,000 ÷ 360); trap wrong-rule) and 0.14 years / or 136.9 days; or keep 73 and explain it as 5,475,000 ÷ 75,000 (misplaced decimal, trap distractor-number).

issue: Trap label 'partial-computation' is used for distractors on non-computational items, where the misconception is an incomplete or overly narrow rule.
evidence: pl-01 (a) 'Only at the overall review stage'; pl-11 (a) 'Understated cost of goods sold only'; pl-12 (b) 'Presentation of receivables only'; pl-16 (c) 'Only the audit budget and fee'; pl-17 (d) 'Only management's representations'; pl-19 (c) 'Only inventory understatement'. None involves a computation; pl-01, 11, 12, 16, 17 are not calc items.
fix: Relabel these as 'overgeneralization' / 'wrong-rule' (or add an 'incomplete-rule' trap type) so trap analytics are not skewed.

issue: Answer cues: the key is the only hedged option against absolute distractors, or distractors overlap/duplicate each other so they can be eliminated without the rule.
evidence: pl-01: (a) 'Only…', (b) 'Only…', (c) 'At all three stages' vs key (d) unqualified. pl-08: (a) 'No risk exists', (c) 'must', (d) 'can't… every' vs key 'possible misstatement'. x2-02: (a) 'No risk', (c) 'must be understated' vs key 'possible misstatement'. pl-19: (c) 'Only inventory understatement' is a subset of key (d) 'COGS overstated…' (understated ending inventory overstates COGS) — overlapping options. pl-26: (a) 'Keep the original amount' and (d) 'Ignore the change' are the same answer, so both fall together.
fix: Give each item at least one hedged, plausible distractor (e.g., pl-08 'The difference is explained by the wage increase, so no work is needed'; x2-02 'The margin is plausible because volume rose'); replace pl-19 (c) with 'Revenue overstated' variant or 'Inventory overstated'; replace pl-26 (d) with 'Keep materiality but lower performance materiality only'.

issue: Implausible distractors make these items near-giveaways, inconsistent with their difficulty labels (pl-25 and x2-04 are the only reasonable choice at a glance).
evidence: pl-09: cash balance / number of shareholders / total assets as a room-revenue expectation. pl-14: 'rely without testing', 'exclude the derivatives', 'issue a disclaimer immediately'. pl-25 (analysis, difficulty 3): 'Better controls', 'Lower fraud risk', 'Normal variation' for a 30%→42% margin jump with no business change. x2-04: 'It must exclude the engagement partner'.
fix: Use CPA-style plausible alternatives: pl-09 'Last year's room revenue adjusted for CPI'; pl-14 'Use the client's valuation specialist's report as audit evidence without evaluating it' / 'Plan to rely on management's representation'; pl-25 'A favourable sales-mix shift' as a plausible-but-unsupported option; x2-04 'It is held once, at the start, and need not be revisited'. Or lower pl-25 to difficulty 1.

issue: Seven of the 27 practice items (26%) test content the aud-planning lesson never teaches and that is taught only in later modules, so learners meet them untaught and misses route back to a lesson that cannot help.
evidence: Lesson body and takeaways contain no materiality, performance materiality, component/group materiality, misstatement accumulation or interim-testing content (grep). Materiality items pl-21, 22, 24, 26 and AU-C 450 item pl-27 belong to aud-risk-materiality (the next module, aud-u3); group-audit item pl-15 to aud-using-others (aud-u8, AUD-III); interim substantive testing pl-18 to aud-risk-response (aud-u5, whose lesson teaches it at lines 86-88). aud-pl-17 (AU-C 510) is at least taught in the earlier aud-engagement-acceptance module.
source: content/sections/aud.yaml module order; lessons of aud-risk-materiality, aud-using-others, aud-risk-response
fix: Move pl-15 to aud-using-others, pl-18 to aud-risk-response and pl-21/22/24/26/27 to aud-risk-materiality (or delete those that duplicate aud-rm items — see the duplication finding), and replace them with planning items the lesson supports: strategy-vs-plan classification scenarios, analytics with nonfinancial drivers, absence-of-expected-change cases, TCWG planning communication, team discussion content.

issue: Redundancy: the single fact 'strategy = scope, timing, direction; plan = nature, timing, extent' is tested by seven MCQs (plus pre1, chk1 and flashcard f1), several as mirror images; mock item x2-01 reuses chk1's distractor almost verbatim.
evidence: pl-13 'Which element sets the scope, timing and direction?' → strategy; pl-23 'What does the overall audit strategy set?' → scope, timing and direction (exact reverse). pl-16 'What does the detailed audit plan describe?' → NTE; x2-36 'part of the detailed plan rather than the strategy' → NTE. x2-01 (b) 'Selecting the specific invoices to vouch for sales cutoff testing' ≈ chk1 (b) 'The specific invoices to vouch for sales cut-off'. Same fact, same way, >3 times.
fix: Keep pl-13 and x2-36; replace pl-16 and pl-23 with application items (e.g., which change requires updating the overall strategy vs. only the plan; planning direction, supervision and review; initial-engagement planning under AU-C 300.13); give x2-01 new distractors not used in the lesson check.

issue: Cross-module near-duplicates: these practice items repeat items in other modules, in two cases with identical numbers.
evidence: pl-26 ($2,000,000 planned → $1,200,000 actual pretax income; lower materiality) ≈ aud-rm-14 (same $2,000,000 / $1,200,000, key 'Revise it to $60,000') and aud-rm-07. pl-11 'Inventory turnover fell from 8 times to 5 times while sales were stable' ≈ aud-inv-24 'Inventory turnover fell from 8 to 5 while sales stayed flat' (same key). pl-24 (5% × $2,000,000) ≈ mock item aud-x2-25 (same 5% × $2,000,000 base) and aud-rm-05. pl-21 ≈ aud-rm-04 (pretax income benchmark). pl-22 ≈ aud-rm-16 and aud-rm-chk2 (PM lower than materiality).
fix: Delete pl-21, pl-22, pl-24 and pl-26 (aud-risk-materiality already covers them) and rewrite pl-11 with different facts (e.g., DSI, or turnover falling while sales rose) or drop it.

issue: Mock-exam duplication: aud-x2-04 and aud-x2-46 (aud-understanding-entity) sit in the same testlet of aud-mock-3 and test the same fact with the same key; aud-x2-39 on aud-mock-3 is a near-verbatim copy of the lesson check aud-pl-chk2.
evidence: aud-mock-3 testlet 2 contains both aud-x2-46 ('…engagement team discussion… correct?' key 'It covers how fraud might occur in the statements') and aud-x2-04 ('…engagement team discussion is correct?' key 'It should cover how fraud could occur in the statements'). aud-x2-39 ('Which procedure is not a risk assessment procedure?' options inquiry / analytics / observation-inspection / confirming AR, key d) = aud-pl-chk2 options and key. One mock item reveals the other; the mock rewards memory of the lesson check.
fix: Replace aud-x2-04 on aud-mock-3 (or rewrite it to test another aspect, e.g., who must participate or when the discussion is revisited); rewrite aud-pl-chk2 with different procedures (e.g., 'reading minutes vs. recomputing depreciation') so the mock item is not pre-exposed.

issue: This substantive-analytical-procedure TBS is mapped to aud-planning (unit aud-u3, AUD-II), but substantive analytics (expectation, threshold, investigate the difference) are AUD-III content taught in aud-data-analytics and aud-risk-response; the aud-planning lesson only says substantive analytics are optional.
evidence: TBS title 'Substantive analytical procedures'; moduleIds ['aud-planning'], unitId aud-u3. The threshold/investigation steps are taught in aud-data-analytics lesson lines 111-114 and aud-risk-response (rr-chk2, rr-10, rr-13, rr-18). aud-planning lesson never mentions thresholds. Coverage counts this TBS under AUD-II, and misses route to a lesson that does not teach it.
fix: Change moduleIds to ['aud-data-analytics'] (unitId aud-u6) or ['aud-risk-response'] (aud-u5).

issue: Skill and time are overstated: the task is three one-step multiplications, three subtractions and three threshold comparisons (labelled analysis, 20 minutes).
evidence: ie 8,000,000 × 6% = 480,000; pe 120 × 55,000 = 6,600,000; de 12,000,000 ÷ 10 = 1,200,000; differences 60,000 / 50,000 / 300,000 vs. thresholds 25,000 / 100,000 / 60,000. No explanations to evaluate, no precision or data-reliability judgment. Realistic time ≈ 8-10 minutes; skill = application ('perform substantive analytical procedures').
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions; AU-C 520.05
fix: Relabel skill application and minutes 10, or add analysis rows (e.g., management's explanation of the interest difference — a mid-year $1M drawdown — to corroborate; whether to investigate the whole difference or the excess; expectation precision).

issue: The dropdown part's row labels give away the numeric part's answers (gross margin 36%, allowance 2%, days in inventory 91).
evidence: Row k1 'Gross margin rose to 36%…' = gm key 36.0; k2 'allowance fell from 5% to 2%…' = alw key 2.0; k3 'Days in inventory rose from 73 to 91 days' ≈ dsi key 91.3. Both parts are in one simulation, so a candidate can copy three of the four numeric answers.
source: Review brief §2 per-TBS checks (exhibits/answers consistent; no cues)
fix: Make the risk rows qualitative ('The gross margin movement compared with the industry', 'The allowance coverage trend', 'The days-in-inventory trend'), or show the numeric results only after part r is submitted.

issue: Row k1 (margin up to 36%): 'Inventory — valuation' is a plausible competing answer that the explanation does not address; the exhibit's clean 'inventory costing' test does not clearly cover lower-of-cost-and-NRV, and k3 shows slow-moving stock.
evidence: An unrecorded obsolescence write-down understates cost of sales and inflates margin. Size check (python): to lift margin from 30% to 36% on 9,125,000 sales, COGS would have to be understated by 547,500 = 37.5% of year-end inventory 1,460,000 — implausible as a missed write-down, whereas fictitious sales of ~782,000 explain both the margin and DSO 40→60. So Revenue — occurrence is best, but the explanation only rules out 'Cost of sales — completeness'.
fix: Add a sentence to k1's explanation: 'A missed inventory write-down would also lift the margin, but it would need to be about $548,000 (37.5% of inventory), and the receivables build-up points to revenue.' Optionally say in the exhibit that the NRV review is not yet done (which keeps k3 = valuation).

issue: Worked example 'Scanning the ratios' compares a Year 2 inventory turnover on average inventory (3.6) with a Year 1 turnover on year-end inventory (4.0), teaching an inconsistent comparison.
evidence: python: Y2 2,847,000 ÷ 800,000 avg = 3.56; Y1 2,810,500 ÷ 700,000 year-end = 4.02; like-for-like Y2 on year-end inventory 2,847,000 ÷ 900,000 = 3.16. Every other worked number checks: GM 35.0% vs 30.0%; DSO 50.0 vs 36.4 days; faded block 20,000 / 50 / 30 days.
fix: Compute both years on year-end inventory (3.2 vs 4.0 times) — matching aud-tbs-u3-analytics, which uses year-end inventory — and drop the 'Year 1 average not available' caveat.

issue: The lesson says only the audit plan is updated during the audit; AU-C 300 requires updating both the overall strategy and the plan (and item aud-pl-10 keys 'revise the strategy and plan').
evidence: Takeaway: 'The plan is more detailed and is updated throughout the audit.' Timeline: 'Audit plan — Updated whenever new information changes the risk assessment.' The strategy rows carry no such note. AU-C 300.10: the auditor should update and change the overall audit strategy and the audit plan as necessary during the audit.
fix: Reword the takeaway: 'Both the strategy and the plan are updated as necessary throughout the audit; the plan is the more detailed of the two.' Add the same note to the timeline's strategy event.

issue: Correct-choice explanation 'The risk of material misstatement is higher' misstates why: accumulated misstatements approaching materiality raise the risk that undetected plus accumulated misstatements exceed materiality (aggregation/detection side), not the entity's RMM; it also omits asking management to correct.
evidence: AU-C 450.08(b): determine whether the overall strategy and plan need revision when the aggregate of accumulated misstatements approaches materiality; AU-C 450.A? application guidance: a greater than acceptably low risk that possible undetected misstatements, with those accumulated, could exceed materiality. Item text: (d) explanation 'Correct. The risk of material misstatement is higher.'
fix: Change to: 'Correct. AU-C 450: when accumulated misstatements approach materiality, the risk that undetected misstatements push the total over materiality is too high, so the auditor revisits the strategy and plan, performs more procedures, and may ask management to correct the misstatements found.'

issue: Thin or off-target choice explanations: they do not state the rule or name the error.
evidence: pl-16 key (a) explanation 'Correct. The strategy sets the overall scope.' explains the strategy, not why NTE is the plan. pl-17 key (b) 'Correct. AU-C 510.' (citation only). pl-20 distractors: (b) 'Compound the changes.', (c) 'Include the rate increase.', (d) 'Include headcount growth.' — instructions, not the error (b = additive 5% + 3% = 8%; c = headcount only; d = rate only).
fix: pl-16 (a): 'Correct. AU-C 300.09: the plan describes the nature, timing and extent of risk assessment and further audit procedures.' pl-17 (b): 'Correct. AU-C 510.08: obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period, and whether policies were applied consistently.' pl-20: '(b) adds 5% + 3% = 8% instead of 1.05 × 1.03; (c) applies only headcount growth; (d) applies only the rate increase.'

issue: Key text 'Setting the engagement's framework, deadlines, and scope' implies the auditor sets the financial reporting framework; the strategy identifies the engagement's characteristics, such as the framework management uses.
evidence: AU-C 300.08(a) / A-guidance: the strategy identifies the characteristics of the engagement that define its scope, such as the financial reporting framework used; the framework is chosen by management.
fix: Reword to 'Identifying the reporting framework, reporting deadlines, and scope of the engagement'.

issue: The lesson omits two AU-C 300 planning requirements a Blueprint II.A task names: planning the nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review (AU-C 300.11), and the extra planning activities for an initial audit (AU-C 300.13, e.g., communication with the predecessor).
evidence: grep of lesson: no 'supervis', 'review of their work', 'initial audit' or 'predecessor'. blueprint-tasks.csv AUD-II.A.2 (reconstructed): 'Prepare the engagement strategy and plan, including the nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review.' Direction/supervision is mentioned only in aud-quality-management (SAS 146 partner responsibilities).
source: AU-C 300.11, 300.13; AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint Area II.A
fix: Add a short section 'Planning supervision and review; initial audits' (2-3 bullets) and one practice item on each.

issue: The lesson has one pre-question (strategy vs. plan detail) and teaches inventory turnover but not days in inventory or allowance coverage; the module's analysis objective (planning analytics) is not primed, and two ratios used in aud-tbs-u3-analytics are never shown.
evidence: preQuestions: [aud-pl-pre1] only. aud-tbs-u3-analytics asks for days sales in inventory (inventory ÷ (COGS ÷ 365)) and allowance as % of receivables; the lesson's worked example covers gross margin, DSO and turnover only.
fix: Add a second pre-question on an analytics signal (e.g., 'margin up while industry fell — which accounts would you look at?') and one line in the worked example: 'Days in inventory = 365 ÷ turnover (or inventory ÷ daily COGS)'; mention allowance coverage in the risk step.
